name: reading-quiz
what: A reader holding only the skill, its references and its two agents answers what the text requires at its densest points. Each wrong option differs from the right one in one detail; the options are shuffled per question by its id.

questions.q: A reconciliation runs without `--audit`. Which pairs does `--stage` hand no judge as current?
options: A pair whose binding computes at the file's content as it stands, with no open finding against it in the corpus
A pair whose binding computes at the file's content as it stands, whether or not a finding is open against it
A pair whose node's text did not move since the bind, whatever the file's content
Every pair of a file the drift report does not list

questions.q: The person asks to re-examine standing bindings that never drifted. What runs?
options: `--stage --audit`: every pair goes to a judge, and no candidate tier is staged or passed
`--stage --audit`: every pair goes to a judge, and the candidate index is passed as usual
`--stage` without `--audit`: the guard omits nothing where nothing drifted
`--stage --audit`, chosen by the skill whenever `--check` reports no drift on the set

questions.q: How does each conformance judge receive the candidate index?
options: As its absolute, resolved path; never its contents
As its contents, pasted into each prompt so the judge need not open a file
As its path relative to the target source root, for the judge to resolve
As its absolute path, handed only to a judge whose file states an unstated fact

questions.q: The person names nodes `/analyse` wrote after the source was last bound. What happens to them?
options: Each is passed to `--stage` with `--node`; it joins the candidate tier and cannot be bound here
Each is passed to `--stage` with `--node`, and bound where its judge clears it
The skill finds them itself from the specification's history since the bind
Each is added to its file's node pack, read like a bound node

questions.q: When is the next wave of judges spawned?
options: After `--save-return` reports `0 pending` for the current wave, read from the returns on disk
After the session has counted one notification per judge of the current wave
Immediately: every wave is spawned in one message and the saves follow
After `--save-return` reports `0 pending` for every wave the staging listed

questions.q: The harness refuses a judge's launch. What follows?
options: The wave was cut too wide: the report hands `--stage --concurrency <fewer>`, and no judge is dispatched again on the invocation's own account
The wave was cut too wide: the refused judge is dispatched again in the next turn
The refused file is judged inline, and the report says the pass ran inline
The wave was cut too wide: the report hands `--stage --concurrency <fewer>`, and the refused judge is dispatched once more first

questions.q: Where and how is a judge's return saved?
options: Verbatim at `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns/<path with '/' as '__'>.yaml`; `--save-return` copies it from a spawned subagent's transcript
Verbatim at `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns/<path with '/' as '__'>.yaml`, retyped from the notification that relays it
Trimmed to the contract's five keys, at `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns/<path with '/' as '__'>.yaml`
Verbatim in the workspace beside the node pack, which the fold reads

questions.q: A saved return carries a sixth key, `notes`, beside the five the contract admits. What happens?
options: `--fold` refuses, and refuses whole; what a subagent says outside the five keys belongs in the report
`--fold` drops the extra key and folds the rest
`--fold` refuses that file's return alone and folds the others
You delete the key from the saved return and fold again

questions.q: A node's judges read its fact in one file and answered `nowhere` for another of its bound files, with nothing found against it. What does the bind do?
options: Binds the node on the file that holds it; the bind's receipt hands the `nowhere` pair's `--release ... --node` ready, relayed as the person's decision
Binds the node on the file that holds it, and releases the `nowhere` pair itself
Binds nothing for the node until the `nowhere` pair is released
Binds the node on the file that holds it; the report hands a `--replace` naming the files to keep

questions.q: The report lists a node the judgment did not clear that carries `collateral`. What does it mean?
options: Nothing was found against its substance: it shares a file with a finding that named no node, and its route rides that finding's
A finding named it in a sibling file, and its route is its own `/analyse` door
Nothing was found against its substance, so the bind writes it anyway
It shares a file with a finding that named no node, and the report hands it its own `/plan-work` door
Only the pairs under some node's `encoded_at`; a file an earlier bind put on the node and the record does not name stays bound
Only the pairs under some node's `encoded_at`; a file an earlier bind put on the node and the record does not name is dropped
The whole set, once the judgment cleared most of its nodes
Every node of the record, cleared or not, each stamped with its outcome

questions.q: The person says a fact moved out of a file rather than into an additional one. What does the skill do with `--replace`?
options: Never passes it: the report hands that invocation ready to paste, and stops
Passes it on the bind, since the person stated the move
Never passes it, and never hands it either: the release is the only route
Passes it after reading the bind's receipt of what stopped being claimed

questions.q: The person offers a test as a node's proof. How is it certified?
options: Written into a YAML passed as `--certify`; a coverage auditor reads the certification pack, the file's conformance judge runs too, and the fold writes `decided_by: test` only from `covered`
Written into a YAML passed as `--certify`; the coverage auditor replaces the file's conformance judge for that node
The skill picks the tests that exercise the node from the project's suite and certifies them
Written into a YAML passed as `--certify`; the fold writes `decided_by: test` wherever the node's type is one a test decides

questions.q: The staging separated pairs under `mechanical`. How is step 3b run, and what if a step is red?
options: `run.py siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns --run <slug>` with the registry's commands, once; a red step is a result the fold reads, never re-run
`run.py siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns --run <slug>`; a red step is re-run under the same name until it is green
`run.py <workspace> --run <slug>`, once; a red step is a result the fold reads
`run.py siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns --run <slug>` with commands composed from the tree's layout, once

questions.q: The person stated a rewrite, and the staging's receipt says it reproduces nothing. What now?
options: Stop and show the person the transcription before any judge runs
Continue: every drifted pair goes to a judge as without the rewrite
Adjust the pattern until it reproduces the current text, then stage again
Stage again under the same slug without `--rewrite`

questions.q: When does an invocation run as an adoption?
options: Only where the person names the mode; the candidates are theirs to name, and a test file in the set is refused with the `--certify` entry it takes
Whenever no trace file exists for the target; the candidates are the person's to name
Only where the person names the mode; a test file in the set is adopted as source beside the rest
Only where the person names the mode; the candidates are the nodes the specification holds under the files' areas

questions.q: Where does the file set come from?
options: The person names every path, each relative to the target source root; it is never discovered
The `code` lines `trace.py --check` prints, kept where the person named a directory
The person names every path, each relative to the git toplevel, as `trace.py` prints it
The person names the paths, and the skill adds every file that shares a node with them

questions.q: A judge found `contradicts` against a node. What does the report hand?
options: Both the `/analyse` and the `/plan-work` doors, with what each assumes and what would settle it; choosing is the person's own decision
The `/analyse` door, recommended, since the source is newer than the node
The `/plan-work` door, recommended, since the node is the authority
Both doors, and the comment route recommended over them by `rule violated`
